candidate.name: operating_procedure_overlay
candidate.hypothesis: Appending a turn-invariant operating-procedure overlay to the system message will reduce invalid device-tool calls and premature terminations, raising pass rate above the 0.18 identity baseline without increasing token or turn cost.
candidate.changes: Single mechanism: AgentHarness.transform_request idempotently appends a marker-delimited procedure block to the first system message of the model request (a new system message is prepended only when none exists; transform_response and register() stay identity). The overlay states: (1) only schema tools are callable - policy device functions run on the customer's device and must be requested from the customer in plain language, one action at a time, waiting for confirmation; (2) account/line identifiers must be resolved from customer-provided information, never guessed or applied to another line; (3) do not declare resolution, transfer, or end the conversation while any suspected cause is unaddressed - revisit both device-side settings and account-side state before repeating a failed fix. Shape-robust and fail-safe: handles dict/object/bare-list requests, str or content-part messages, degrades to identity on any unexpected shape. No task names, IDs, per-instance data, evaluator access, or cross-episode state.
candidate.expected_efficiency: Tokens flat to lower (overlay adds ~0.2k tokens per request, but targets the 226/872 = 26% of tool results that were 'Tool not found' errors); turns roughly flat, with premature transfers (21/41 failed runs) converted into continued troubleshooting.

candidate.name: device_intent_relay
candidate.hypothesis: The solver repeatedly emits calls to out-of-schema functions that the customer's device executes (3.3 attempts and 3.5 'Tool not found' errors per episode, 167 attempts over 50 baseline runs) and frequently gives up after such dead turns (8 transfers within 4 messages of an error; 18 runs where the customer performed zero device actions). Rewriting exactly those turns into one explicit single-step plain-language request addressed to the customer, before the environment can reject them, will convert device-never-requested and give-up-after-error failures into customer-executed device fixes and lift pass rate above the 0.18 identity baseline, without increasing cumulative tokens by more than ~15%.
candidate.changes: Single mechanism at the response boundary. transform_response(response, public_history) locates the assistant message payload (dict/object/list shapes, including choices[0].message nesting and flattened call form), classifies each tool call by name against the schema-captured account tool names (transform_request records them, identity otherwise; tau2 TelecomTools public names are the schema-unseen fallback), and gates relay candidacy to the customer-device vocabulary via tau2.domains.telecom.user_tools.TelecomUserTools when importable. A turn made up entirely of relay candidates has tool_calls set to None, the model's own text preserved, and exactly one appended request ('I can't reach your device directly - please do this on your phone and tell me what you see: <action>'); the action string is rendered purely lexically from the function name with a small general-English verb map plus any parsed arguments, extra candidates are dropped (one action at a time), and a per-episode counter switches repeats of the same function to confirmation phrasing ('If you have already done that, just tell me what your phone shows now: ...') to prevent double toggles. Mixed turns drop only the relay candidates and keep valid calls in order with ids intact; turns without relay candidates are untouched. register() stays identity. Fail-safe by construction: unrecognized shapes, non-writable payloads, exceptions, or a failed read-back after mutation restore the original response untouched. No task names, IDs, per-instance tables, evaluator access, model/network/filesystem/subprocess calls, or cross-episode state; only per-instance counters.
candidate.expected_efficiency: Prompt tokens +6-12% per episode (~297k -> 315-335k cumulative) from the appended relay messages, completion tokens +5-10%; 'Tool not found' tool results per episode 3.5 -> ~0; messages per run 47.5 -> 52-58 as dead turns are replaced by customer-visible actions. Expected pass rate 0.18 -> 0.26-0.34 by converting device-never-requested, premature give-up, and dead-end-output failures; account-side last-mile errors (wrong identifiers, refuel/enable_roaming never called) are out of scope for this mechanism.

candidate.name: primary_line_binding
candidate.hypothesis: In recorded episodes the solver acts on the first line listed in customer-lookup results (190/190 lookups return the same account with an unrelated line first; 38 wrong-line detail reads vs 6 on the caller's line; 7 refuel/roaming calls aimed at the wrong line while every expected device action already matched). If the lookup returns the record with the line matching the queried number moved to the front of its line list, the solver's first-line heuristic will target the caller's own line, converting wrong-line account failures into passes and lifting the 50-task pass rate from 0.22 to at least 0.28, with flat turns and tokens.
candidate.changes: Single mechanism at the account-tool boundary. The module exports an identity AgentHarness (as in baseline_zero: __init__(public_context=None), transform_request/transform_response return their inputs) plus register(), which installs exactly one class-level wrapper on the plain tau2 TelecomTools.get_customer_by_phone. The wrapper calls the original (lookup errors propagate), then, on a non-None Customer, finds the first entry in customer.line_ids whose line's phone_number matches the queried number after digit-only normalization (resolved via the toolkit's own _get_line_by_id, unresolvable entries skipped); if found and not already first, it returns a shallow copy of the record (model_copy(deep=False), copy.copy fallback, identity-checked) whose line_ids is rebound to a new list with the matched line first and the rest in relative order. The live account object and its list are never mutated, so DB state is untouched; reordering is order-preserving for every internal use (iteration and membership only). Every other path (None result, shorter than two lines, no match, already first, unexpected shape, any exception) returns the original result unchanged. functools.wraps plus an explicit matching signature keep the tool schema identical; installation is idempotent via a marker attribute and is a harmless no-op when tau2 is absent. The previous round's inert response-relay code is removed (its prefix string appears 0 times across all recorded episodes). No task names/IDs, instance-specific tables, evaluator access, extra model/network/subprocess/filesystem calls, or cross-episode state; imports are stdlib copy/functools plus a guarded tau2 import.
candidate.expected_efficiency: Tokens flat to slightly lower (within ~5%): the same lookups are issued, but detail reads and account actions land on the caller's line instead of being spent on an unrelated line first; turns flat; no change to device-side traffic. Evidence of the target: 0/24 expected refuel actions and 0/17 expected roaming actions have matched on the caller's line so far, with 7+ direct wrong-line counterfactual episodes reachable.

candidate.name: caller_line_digest
candidate.hypothesis: In the incumbent's 35 failing episodes, refuel_data is expected in 24 but attempted in 0 of the 18 episodes where it is missed, because no single read states the plan's allowance - line reads expose data_used_gb only (7 of those 18 read the caller's line yet the model reasons 'The plan details are not provided ... which is under the limit unless the plan's data limit is low'); and 12 of 35 failing episodes read a sibling line because the earlier first-line reorder does not bind the solver to the caller's line on its own. If line-shaped reads carry the derived over-limit fact and the caller-line association, the solver can see when refueling is due and which line is the caller's, converting at least 2 of those account-side failures into passes and lifting the 50-task pass rate from 0.30 to >= 0.34 with flat turns and <= 3% token increase.
candidate.changes: Single mechanism at the account-tool boundary: materialize already-derivable facts into line-read observations. The module keeps the incumbent's identity AgentHarness and extends register() with class-level wrappers on the plain tau2 TelecomTools. (1) The existing get_customer_by_phone wrapper still resolves the line whose number matches the query and returns the record with that line first on a shallow copy (live account untouched); it now also remembers, once per toolkit instance, that line id (fallback: the record's own contact number when it uniquely identifies one line; ambiguous or unresolvable -> nothing remembered; first successful resolution wins, never overwritten; instance attribute only, so no cross-episode state). (2) New wrapper on get_details_by_id: after the original call (errors propagate), only line-shaped results (has line_id, plan_id, data_used_gb) are converted to a plain dict via model_dump(mode='json')/dict() and enriched with plan_data_limit_gb, data_limit_exceeded (used >= limit + refueled, only when all three are finite numbers), and, when the caller's line is known, is_customer_line / customer_line_id; Customer/Device/Bill/Plan results and every unexpected shape return the original object. (3) New wrapper on get_data_usage: returns a copy of the usage dict with data_limit_exceeded and the same association keys, or the original dict on any surprise. All branches are fail-safe (identity on missing attributes, plan-miss, non-numeric values, or any exception), functools.wraps plus matching signatures keep the tool schemas byte-identical, each wrapper has its own idempotency marker, and register() stays a harmless no-op without tau2. The dict return is safe because the harness serializes non-str results with json.dumps(result, default=str) (source_view/harness_base_protocol.py _serialize_tool_result) and tau2's Environment passes str results through unchanged. Imports are stdlib copy/functools plus the existing guarded tau2 import. No task names/IDs, instance-specific tables, evaluator access, extra model/network/subprocess/filesystem calls, or cross-episode state.
candidate.expected_efficiency: Tokens +0.1-0.3% (each enriched line read adds ~40-120 tokens, ~1.5 line reads per episode), turns flat (+-0.5). Expected pass rate 0.30 -> 0.34-0.42 by converting episodes where every device-side action already matched and only the account-side refuel step (or the wrong-line read that precedes it) was missing; the 12/15 already-passing episodes see the same raw values plus a data_limit_exceeded=false flag, so regression risk is low. Episodes that fail only by announcing a transfer without calling the tool are out of scope for this mechanism.

candidate.name: device_call_redirect
candidate.hypothesis: In the incumbent's 35 failing episodes, 25 contain at least one action that the task assigns to the customer and that never happened, and the recorded episodes show the two shapes this takes: the solver attempts the customer-device function itself, the domain answers 'Error: Tool '<name>' not found.', and the solver then either dismisses the fix ('the tool isn't available, so I can't turn it off'), retries the same dead call, or transfers (8 failing episodes attempted, in-schema-style, exactly the action that stayed unperformed; 4 failures transfer with no substantive customer-facing turn at all). Every recorded passing episode instead resolves the same error by immediately telling the customer a concrete manual step, which the customer then performs (e.g. failed 'toggle_airplane_mode' -> 'go to Settings > Network & Internet > Airplane Mode' -> customer turns it off; failed 'reset_apn_settings' -> manual reset steps -> customer resets). If the not-found answer for customer-device names is replaced, at the tool-execution boundary, by a directive that names the action as the customer's own and requires an immediate one-step plain-language request to the customer, the attempted-then-abandoned device fixes convert into customer-performed fixes, lifting the 50-task pass rate from 0.30-0.32 to at least 0.36 with a token change under 0.5%.
candidate.changes: Single mechanism at the unknown-tool boundary of plain tau2 tool execution, on top of the retained primary_line_binding reorder (kept byte-identical). The module keeps the identity AgentHarness (public_context/transform_request/transform_response) and extends register(): (1) it installs, at most once each via a marker on the wrapper and on the original, a functools.wraps wrapper over use_tool on both tau2.domains.telecom.tools.TelecomTools and tau2.domains.telecom.environment.TelecomEnvironment (each behind its own guarded import; either class missing means that wrapper is simply not installed); (2) the wrapper calls the original with the same (tool_name, *args, **kwargs) and returns its result unchanged on success; (3) only when the original raises an exception whose message contains 'not found' and contains the requested tool name, and the name is a customer-device function, it returns a plain string directive in place of the exception - 'Error: Tool '<name>' not found. ... only the customer can do that ... do not give up, do not say it is impossible or unnecessary, do not transfer ... ask them to make this change on their phone, in plain words without tool names, one step at a time, and wait for them to tell you what their phone shows' - with a read-styled variant (check_/get_/is_/list_/can_/run_/view_/read_ prefixes) that asks the customer to look the value up and report it; (4) customer-device names are detected from the public callable names of tau2.domains.telecom.user_tools.TelecomUserTools (guarded import, cached once at register time, small non-tool deny-list) plus a device-only prefix fallback (toggle_/set_/check_/reset_/reboot/unseat_/reseat_/lock_/unlock_/grant_/revoke_/disconnect_/connect_/run_speed_), so a misspelled or unrelated unknown name still gets the untouched generic error; (5) a per-instance counter dict stored on the toolkit or environment instance (never module-global, never shared across episodes) appends one conditional reminder to the write phrasing on a repeated same-name redirect, so a second redirect cannot push the customer into toggling a setting twice, and it is applied only if the attribute can be set; (6) every other path is identity: successes, genuine lookup failures such as a customer not found, non-device names, unexpected exception types, any error raised inside the directive builder (which falls back to re-raising the original), and a missing tau2 (register() stays a harmless no-op); the string return is safe because the harness passes str tool results through unchanged, and the module never touches the DB, never performs an extra tool execution, and makes no network, subprocess, or filesystem calls. Imports are stdlib copy/functools plus the existing guarded tau2 imports. No task names, task IDs, instance-specific tables, expected answers, evaluator access, or cross-episode state.
candidate.expected_efficiency: Tokens +0.1-0.3% (each redirect adds ~55-90 tokens where the recorded episodes show ~4 out-of-schema device calls per episode, writes 81 and reads 129 over 50 episodes); turns flat to +1 (the dead turn is preserved, but its successor becomes a customer request rather than a dismissal, a retry, or a transfer); message count flat. Expected pass rate 0.30-0.32 -> 0.36-0.40 by converting 3-5 of the 8 failing episodes that attempted exactly the action that stayed unperformed, plus part of the deflect/transfer bucket (4 failures end with a transfer and no substantive customer-facing turn), while the 15-16 passing episodes see the same observations plus, on their own failed device calls, the same directive their successful behaviour already implies, so regression risk is bounded to a wrong re-ask, which the repeat reminder guards. Out of scope for this mechanism: the ~17 failing episodes whose missing customer action the solver never attempted at all (a diagnosis gap, not a dead-turn gap), and every account-side-only miss.

candidate.name: caller_line_scope
candidate.hypothesis: On the round-6 batch (50 tasks), the identity baseline and the incumbent primary_line_binding score identically at 0.320 with 0 per-task differences, and every observed phone lookup already lists the matching line first, so the reorder is a no-op here. Batch-3 failures are dominated by line-scope errors: 16 of 34 failing episodes read or write a sibling line (15x enable_roaming L1001, 1x refuel L1001, 14x get_details_by_id L1001, 7x get_data_usage L1001) while passing episodes target the line the caller's own number resolves to (14/16 passes read that line's details; 5/5 refuels are that line, 2.0 GB), and one failing episode even asserts 'the line associated with your phone number (555-123-2001)' while the caller's number is 555-123-2002. Therefore binding account operations requested on a non-caller sibling line of the caller's own account to the line the phone-number lookup resolved will surface the correct line state and land the required change on the asserted line, converting at least 3 of the 34 failures; if fewer than 3 tasks flip, the hypothesis is falsified.
candidate.changes: New single mechanism layered on the retained primary_line_binding file, whose reorder logic is kept byte-identical (same _digit_key, _matching_line_index, _with_line_first, same guarded tau2 import and _mh_primary_line_installed marker). (1) The existing get_customer_by_phone wrapper additionally remembers, per toolkit instance and fully inside its existing try/except, _mh_caller_line_id and _mh_caller_customer_id: the matching line when _matching_line_index finds one, else, when the searched number is the account contact number, the single line whose digit-normalized number equals it; no identification leaves earlier memory untouched, and nothing is stored in module state. (2) A shared helper _caller_sibling_line returns the remembered caller line only when both remembered ids are set, the requested id differs from it, the requested id resolves via _get_line_by_id to a line, the remembered customer still resolves and lists both line ids, and the remembered caller line still resolves; any error or unexpected shape returns None. (3) Five functools.wraps-decorated class-level wrappers, each installed at most once behind a _mh_caller_scope_installed marker with its original captured before assignment: get_details_by_id (id arg, positional 0 / keyword 'id'), get_data_usage, refuel_data, enable_roaming, disable_roaming (line_id, positional 1 / keyword 'line_id'). Each wrapper substitutes the caller line id only when the helper fires, preserves the call shape (positional or keyword) and every other argument (customer_id, gb_amount) untouched, guards only the remap computation (a failure falls back to the untouched args) and calls the original outside that guard so its own exceptions propagate unchanged; results are returned as-is, with no annotations, extra fields, prompt text, or error rewrites. (4) register() installs the lookup wrapper plus the five wrappers, each in its own try/except; with tau2 absent everything is a harmless no-op. Imports are only copy and functools plus the guarded tau2 import; no labels, expected answers, evaluator access, task ids, task-specific tables, hidden state, or cross-episode mutable state.
candidate.expected_efficiency: Tokens and turns flat to -3%: identical tool-call counts and message shapes, only the line-id argument changes, and converted episodes avoid the wrong-line follow-up loops that dominate the 42-86 message failing runs. Expected pass rate 0.32 -> 0.38-0.44 by converting 3-6 of the 34 failures (23/34 failing episodes already perform a sibling-line read or write; 18 carry a roaming trigger and 14 a data_usage_exceeded trigger). Regression risk is bounded: before any phone lookup, on the caller's own line, on non-line ids, on lines outside the remembered account, and on any ambiguity or error, behavior is byte-identical to the retained incumbent.
